rationale: Registered the question of whether a restarted Raft node's own configuration is reconstructed from its committed log, three source-grounded behaviours and one necessary gap, and requested one focused multi-case probe (RestoreCommittedLogs enabled/disabled across two single-voter restart shapes) that records the reconstructed configuration, its persisted origin, election attempts and bounded leadership recovery. The question-level account is source-based plus construction-time local feedback only, so its conclusion and defect judgment stay unresolved until the retained execution is interpreted.

investigations.question: When a node restarts with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over a commit-tracking log store, is the configuration it afterwards uses for elections and for counting committed support the committed configuration recorded in its own log, and what do a divergent reconstruction and the resulting support context do to decisions and progress?
investigations.hypothesis: NewRaft re-derives Raft's own configuration only from configuration-carrying log entries above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied); because restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied to the store's tracked commit index before that scan, a committed configuration entry at or below that index is never re-derived, so the restarted node keeps the configuration installed from snapshot metadata (or none at all when no snapshot exists) and then judges its own eligibility and support against that stale context.
investigations.discriminator: Whether the restarted instance's latest configuration index and server set match the configuration entry persisted in its own log, whether the reconstructed value equals the snapshot metadata's configuration, and whether the identical setup with the flag disabled completes leadership recovery inside the same bounded window.

knowledge.statement: NewRaft re-derives Raft's own configuration from configuration-carrying log entries only for indices above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied); the other writers of r.configurations are snapshot restore, snapshot install and the leader's own appendConfigurationEntry path, and nothing else repairs it.
knowledge.conditions: Startup reconstruction in NewRaft over a log store; lastApplied may already be advanced by restoreFromCommittedLogs or by a restored snapshot; configuration entries are identified by LogConfiguration or the deprecated peer entry types.

knowledge.statement: restoreFromCommittedLogs reads the commit index from a CommitTrackingLogStore, clamps it to the last log index, sets the commit index and calls processLogs, which applies the committed prefix to the FSM and sets lastApplied to that commit index; this happens after snapshot restore and before NewRaft's configuration scan.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the tracked commit index is at least the index of a configuration entry stored in the log.

knowledge.statement: The configuration a node holds decides its own participation and support arithmetic: runFollower declines to campaign when latestIndex is zero or the local ID has no vote in the latest configuration, a candidate needs quorumSize() votes of the latest configuration, and the leader's commitment is constructed from the latest configuration, so a stale or empty reconstruction directly changes which support is required and counted.
knowledge.conditions: The configuration is the one reconstructed at startup or later written by a snapshot install or a configuration change; quorumSize and the commitment are computed from configurations.latest.

knowledge.statement: appendEntries processes configuration entries only for the entries it newly appends; entries already present at the same index and term are skipped, so ordinary replication from a healthy leader does not re-derive the configuration of a follower whose log already matches.
knowledge.conditions: Follower handling a normal AppendEntries whose entries are duplicates of its own log; entries that are in the leader's compacted prefix instead arrive as an InstallSnapshot, which rewrites both configurations from the snapshot metadata.

gaps.question: Does any enabled path repair a restarted node's stale or empty configuration without a later membership change, for example ordinary AppendEntries from a healthy leader that still holds the entries?

interpretations.rationale: Source-based account, no retained receipt yet. NewRaft re-derives the node's own configuration only from configuration-carrying log entries above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied) [scan_start], and with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs over a CommitTrackingLogStore the preceding restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied to the store's tracked commit index [restore_lastapplied, restore_doc], so a committed configuration entry at or below that index is never re-derived and r.configurations keeps whatever restoreSnapshot installed from snapshot metadata [snapshot_cfg] (nothing at all when no snapshot exists). That reconstructed context is what the node then uses: runFollower refuses to campaign when latestIndex is zero or the local ID has no vote [follower_gate], votesNeeded is quorumSize() of the latest configuration [candidate_quorum], and the leader commitment is built from the latest configuration [leader_commitment]. Duplicate entries in an AppendEntries are skipped without reprocessing their configuration entries [append_new], so ordinary replication from a healthy leader does not repair the reconstruction; only a newly appended configuration entry, an installed snapshot, or a restart with the flag disabled rewrites it [install_snapshot_cfg, cfg_entry]. Construction-time local feedback in this workspace (four cases: 1-voter and 2-voter bootstrapped clusters, 100 committed commands, 3000 ms observation window, in-memory transport and in-memory commit-tracking store) matched that account and is not a receipt: with the flag disabled the restarted voter's latest configuration index equalled the configuration entry index persisted in its own log (1 and 103) and it reached Leader promptly in both shapes; with the flag enabled the same restarts produced a latest configuration index of 0 with an empty server set and no election attempt for the whole window (state Follower) in the no-snapshot shape, and a latest configuration index of 1 whose server set equalled the snapshot metadata's two-voter configuration (still containing the peer removed at log index 103, which the node skipped) in the snapshot-then-remove shape, where it stayed Candidate with about forty pre-vote campaigns and no leader. The requested execution compares those observations against the persisted configuration entry under a disabled-flag control; until its receipt exists the conclusion and any defect judgment remain unresolved.
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.
limitations: No retained execution exists yet: the account rests on source inspection plus construction-time local feedback, not on a receipt.
Not exercised: disk-backed commit-tracking stores, crashes during the restart, and any later client membership change or snapshot install that could rewrite the configuration.
The bounded progress observation is a 3000 ms window (60 x ElectionTimeout of 50 ms) over one process; it is not an unbounded liveness proof.

Source-supported but unexecuted: when the skipped committed entries add voters, the reconstructed configuration has fewer voters than the committed one, so quorumSize() and the leader commitment can treat support that is not a majority of the committed configuration as sufficient; that safety direction is not exercised by this probe.

scope.description: Restart reconstruction of a Raft node's own configuration: four in-process cases over the captured package's own test facilities, pairing RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled within two single-voter committed shapes. Each case applies 100 commands through the leader, optionally snapshots and then commits RemoveServer for the non-leader peer, reads the configuration entry and tracked commit index from the surviving instance's own log store, stops every instance, and restarts the surviving voter with NewRaft over the same log, stable and snapshot stores plus a fresh in-memory transport.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across the restart and no other instance is left running to send entries.

In both shapes the committed configuration after the setup is a single-voter configuration: the bootstrap configuration (1 voter) with no snapshot, or a snapshot taken before a committed RemoveServer that leaves 1 voter while the snapshot metadata still holds 2.
The bounded progress window is 3000 ms (60 x ElectionTimeout = 50 ms, HeartbeatTimeout = 50 ms) and the flag-disabled control runs the identical setup for each shape.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, process crashes during the restart, and post-restart client membership changes or snapshot installs that could rewrite the configuration.

experiment.prefix: The single generated test builds each case with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 1 or 2, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), applies 100 commands through the elected leader, and for the second shape calls leader.Snapshot() followed by leader.RemoveServer(non-leader ID) plus 10 more applies. Before the restart it reads, from the surviving instance's own stores, the last configuration-carrying log entry (index, decoded server list) together with the snapshot metadata's ConfigurationIndex and server list and the commit-tracking store's staged commit index; it then shuts down every instance and restarts the survivor with NewRaft over the same stores and a fresh in-memory transport wrapped in a counter for RequestPreVote/RequestVote. Each emitted CA_EVENT JSON line carries scenario and restore_committed_logs as identity, plus raw operands (latest_config_index, log_config_index, snapshot_config_index and the server lists), the instance's own configuration, the public GetConfiguration view, last_applied, the derived config_entry_in_applied_prefix, election attempts and became_leader over the 3000 ms window.
experiment.responsibility: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and the reconstructed configurations.latest is the only input to the node's own election gating, quorumSize and leader commitment; no component outside Raft is required to repair it.

comparisons.description: Control for the no-snapshot shape: with restore committed logs disabled the restarted voter's latest configuration index should equal the index of the configuration entry persisted in its own log.

No-snapshot shape with restore committed logs enabled and the configuration entry inside the applied prefix: the restored instance's latest configuration index is compared with the configuration entry index in its own log.
Control for the snapshot-then-remove shape: with the flag disabled the restarted voter should pick up the configuration entry committed after the snapshot.

Snapshot-then-remove shape with the flag enabled: the configuration entry committed after the snapshot lies inside the applied prefix, and the restarted instance's latest configuration index is compared with it.

Identifies the origin of the reconstructed value: whether the restarted instance's configuration server set equals the configuration carried by its own snapshot metadata rather than the configuration entry in its log.
Control: the restarted sole voter of the no-snapshot shape reaches Leader inside the bounded window when restore committed logs is disabled.
No-snapshot shape with the flag enabled: the restarted sole voter reaches Leader inside the bounded window.
Control: the restarted sole voter of the snapshot-then-remove shape reaches Leader inside the bounded window when the flag is disabled.
Snapshot-then-remove shape with the flag enabled: the restarted sole voter of the committed single-voter configuration reaches Leader inside the bounded window.
